candidates.strategic_justification: Offers a plausible complete setup at $764.99, supported by frozen claims of a conical burr grinder and steam wand. A singleton list avoids substitution toward cheaper offers while retaining an acceptable purchase prospect.
The identifiable Breville offer at $699.99 presents a credible household setup. Broad espresso-brand reputation supports likely acceptance, but attributed revenue is lower.
The $649.99 Impress offers a credible beginner purchase with frozen support for a conical grinder, temperature control and steam wand. Likely acceptance comes with lower revenue.
No offers means no purchase opportunity and zero attributed revenue.

selection_reason: The Kenmore singleton combines higher revenue with a credible prospect of acceptance within the complete $800 budget. This is a qualitative forecast, not an established optimal outcome.
limitations: The Kenmore accessory inventory and actual seller recourse are not established; ordinary included accessories are an assumption permitted by the brief.
Brand and retailer reputation are broad priors, not product-specific reliability or seller guarantees.
Only unchanged selected cards reach the buyer; frozen page facts and these justifications do not.
The explicit game rules specify one provider, so no competing Google offer is assumed.
buyer_belief: Known preferences favor consistent milk drinks, approachable operation, dependability and seller confidence under an $800 total limit. Manual steaming and sequential preparation are acceptable. I assume the buyer will accept a credible conventional household machine with ordinary included accessories and will prefer it to declining, even without spending the entire budget.
